A fun experience if a bit repetitive. Far Cry is about looking at a beautiful location, killing all that can be killed, climb radio towers and dying because you were not stealthy enough.

You can chose different approaches to play the game, stealth at a bigger difficulty is more fun in my opinion as it presents a bigger challenge than just mowing down everything in front of you. Story is pretty much an excuse, villians are not... what I expected. Everyone build up Vaas as this great videogame villian... which you see 4 times only in cutscenes, has a dialog that is not that interesting or meaningful and you end up killing him easily in a QTE sequence. No idea why he is venerated so much, he does not even have a memorable boss fight.

IN general its a fun experience, specially when you let wild animals do your dirty work.

Far Cry 3 is a very good game.

Nice story, great characters and an amazing villain (maybe the best of all time). The story drops of abit towards the end in my opinion and I wont go into spoilers, but its still a very good story. The gameplay is fun and well polished although its not the greatest of PC ports and you might need a slightly more powerful PC than you would expect for a game from 2012.

But overall this is probably the best far cry game out there (it definitely has the best story) and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes great opeworld, story driven first person shooters.

I first played Far Cry 3 back in 2019 and just came back to it now. This time I went all the way and got the platinum trophy.

The platinum journey was enjoyable overall. The story missions and character progression kept me hooked, and I actually really liked Jason’s growth from being overwhelmed at the start to becoming someone who could handle everything the island threw at him. Hunting for trophies did sometimes feel repetitive, especially with collectibles, but it was rewarding to see it all through.

Positives. The island still looks great, and exploring it never really got old. The gameplay loop of stealth, combat, and freedom in how you approach situations is still strong. Vaas is just as memorable as I remembered, and the pacing of his story still works well.

Negatives. Climbing towers and gathering collectibles dragged things down at times. The wildlife can feel more frustrating than immersive when it interrupts fights.

Overall, replaying and getting the plat for Far Cry 3 was worth the time. It reminded me why the game is considered such an important part of the series, and I’d recommend it to anyone interested in going back to experience it.

An incredible installment in the Far Cry franchise. Solid gameplay with some dungeon crawling sprinkled over the main story if you're up for some tomb raiding. Stealth felt rewarding when I didn't feel like going in guns blazing. I won't go into the story too much to avoid spoilers, but I'll just say the characters are all incredible, leaving you with something to contemplate at the end of it all and maybe, just maybe, you might come to understand what the definition of insanity is. ;)

Once you've played the game and acquainted yourself with the cast, I'd recommend revisiting the villains of the story because I believe there is more to them than meets the eye, with a lot more nuance involved. As a hint, pay attention to their monologues - there're some interesting implications in there.

Contrary to most of the games I play, Far Cry 3 wasn't one that I enjoyed on my first playthrough. Yes the characters (all except for Jason Brody and Citra) are easy to get attatched to, but after my second playthrough I have to say that this game is very close to being a masterpiece.
Story means a lot to me in a game, and I can confidently say that this does not dissapoint.... for the most part. You'll see what I mean if you play the game (hint : Vaas). It flows properly and depending on which ending you choose, poses some interesting questions about our existance as humans. Should we choose to do the same thing over and over again and be expecting changes, or change and force the world to bend and accept us?
The shooting mechanic, although slightly repetitive and challenging at times to the point of frustration, is fun, and flashy.
Conquering the radio towers is fun and addictive, and the animations of climbing in and out of things, jumping into water and jumping over obstacles are impressive and immersive.
I'm not one who likes open world games too much, so after I completed the main storyline and completed a few sidequests, I ended my experience.
TL;DR : A great game for those who love action/adventure/open world. If you can get it on sale, do so.

It's fun. But as open world games go, it's meh. Same goes for the story - nearly none of your friends, girlfriend, etc. have any character development and you barely interact with them, yet the whole point of the game is to rescue them all.

Exploring is only slightly rewarding, as you can level up a little faster with the XP it gives you. Stealth is more rewarding than any other play style, as well, as takedowns and remaining undetected give you way more XP. The way the animals interact with the environment is great, too; seeing animals attack out of nowhere can either be really entertaining, or a huge pain in the ass.

All in all, I guess it was okay. Not much replayability, but you get 30+ hours of fun.

Great adventure story that takes place in the exotic confines of a small island chain in the South Pacific. A group of young vacationing Americans are taken captive by modern day pirates who intend to sell them as slaves to wealthy customers around the globe. After the pirates kill his older brother the protagonist - Jason Brody - seeks to find and free his younger brother and friends. The villains are well drawn - especially the mad pirate Vaas. The combat system is well designed and offers a satisfying variety of weapons for use against not only the pirates but the dangerous native wildlife. This is a game that has aged well and continues to satisfy after many play throughs.

I bought and enjoyed Blood Dragon first, and figured this would be essentially more Blood Dragon. It was not. The game does not benefit from increased scope. Exploring the world becomes tedious quickly, and the single player missions feel very bland and restrictive.

Far Cry 3 is still an amazing open world shooter, with one of the best- and well-known Villains, a huge, and very pretty map, great gunplay, tons of side missions and activities and lots to explore and find.
If you haven’t played this one and you enjoy first person shooters, you own it to yourself to give it a go. Some things seem silly now 13years after its release, and while the game loses some traction in the last third of its runtimes, it is a great, action filled and fun experience from start to finish.
The best FarCry game. Number 4 is great too (before the franchise loses its way) but that gets to kinda stand on the shoulders of this, the 3rd installment.

tldr.text: Very Positive (84%): players praise the story and characters, and the gameplay and combat.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes, which 19% of reviews mention.

details.text: Recent reviews are more likely to report freezes and crashes, with 30% mentioning bugs against 19% overall, so buyers should check recent feedback.
Players who reviewed after a short stretch of play are far less positive than veterans, with 47% of them positive.
